name: Dumbbell Seated Shoulder Press
grip: Pronated or semi-pronated grip holding dumbbells at shoulder level with forearms vertical and wrists stacked.
description: Press two dumbbells overhead from shoulder height while seated upright against a high bench backrest, developing anterior and lateral deltoid mass with back support.
setup: Set an adjustable bench to an upright position (approximately 75 to 85 degrees to support the spine without excessive cervical strain).
Sit firmly with your hips and upper back pressed against the backrest pad, feet flat on the floor.
Kick the dumbbells up to shoulder height using your knees, holding them with palms facing forward or angled slightly inward (scapular plane), forearms vertical.
instructions: Press both dumbbells upward and slightly inward overhead in a smooth, converging vertical path.
Extend your arms fully overhead with elbows softly unlocked at the top without banging the dumbbells together.
Pause for a brief count at the lockout, feeling tension in the deltoids.
Lower the dumbbells slowly under complete control back to ear or shoulder level before starting the next repetition.
cues: Keep forearms vertical under the dumbbells.
Press upward in the natural scapular plane (~30° forward).
Keep upper back and glutes against the pad.
commonMistakes: Flaring elbows completely out to 90 degrees in the coronal plane, causing shoulder impingement.
Arching the lower back excessively off the bench to turn the exercise into an incline chest press.
Banging the dumbbells together at the top of the press.

logging.example: Two 22 kg dumbbells: record 22 kg per dumbbell.
logging.note: Record the mass of an individual dumbbell rather than the combined total pair mass.

variantNote: Seated dumbbell overhead press with back support. Eliminates standing balance demands to focus maximal overload on deltoids while allowing independent arm movement.
